user.title: JUNG HOME over Bluetooth
user.description: Home Assistant joins your JUNG HOME mesh directly over Bluetooth using the network export of the JUNG HOME app, which contains the mesh keys. Choose where the export comes from.

menu_options.gateway: Fetch it from the JUNG HOME Gateway
menu_options.path: Use a file on the Home Assistant host

bluetooth_confirm.title: Is this your JUNG HOME installation?
bluetooth_confirm.description: A JUNG HOME Bluetooth Mesh proxy of network {network_id} is in range. Home Assistant offers every JUNG HOME installation it sees, also a neighbour's. Continue only if this is your installation; you are then asked for the app's mesh export.

zeroconf_confirm.title: JUNG HOME Gateway found
zeroconf_confirm.description: A JUNG HOME Gateway announces itself at {host}. Continue to fetch the JUNG HOME app's network export from it: you then enter its network-key password, or approve an access request in the app. As for an address you type, its certificate is pinned at first contact before anything is sent. Setting up from the discovered gateway is unverified on air.

gateway.title: Fetch the export from the JUNG HOME Gateway
gateway.description: The gateway holds a copy of the app's network export. Enter its address and either its network-key password (from the JUNG HOME app) for immediate access, or leave the password empty and approve the access request in the app after you continue (Settings → Gateway → Access permissions → Open requests, within three minutes; it appears as “{user_name}”). The export is stored under `junghome_ble/` in the Home Assistant configuration directory. It contains every mesh key, like the phone export — keep backups of that directory private.

data_description.gateway_host: IP address or hostname of the JUNG HOME Gateway. A gateway Home Assistant found on the network is filled in already. Otherwise the default `junghome.local` works on many networks, or use its IP address (shown in the app under Settings → Gateway).
data_description.gateway_password: Optional. With it the gateway grants access immediately; without it you approve the request in the app.

gateway_register.title: Waiting for approval in the JUNG HOME app

gateway_refetch.title: Fetch the export again
gateway_refetch.description: Fetches the current network export from the gateway at {host} with the stored access. If the gateway no longer accepts it, you are asked to approve a new access request in the app.

upload.title: Upload the app's export file
upload.description: In the JUNG HOME app open Project → Share via file and send yourself the `JungHome.json` it creates, then upload it here. It is stored under `junghome_ble/` in the Home Assistant configuration directory. It contains every mesh key — keep backups of that directory private.

data_description.export_file: `JungHome.json` from the app (Share via file) or `MeshNetwork.json` from an iOS backup.

path.title: Use a file on the Home Assistant host
path.description: Copy the app's `JungHome.json` (Project → Share via file; includes your device names) or `MeshNetwork.json` (iOS backup) to the Home Assistant host first and enter its path.

data_description.cdb_path: Absolute path on the Home Assistant host, e.g. `/config/junghome/JungHome.json`.
data_description.metadata_dir: Optional, only for `MeshNetwork.json` from an iOS backup: the app's `Application Support` folder with `device_metadata.json` and `scene_metadata.json`, so entities get the names you gave them in the app. `JungHome.json` already carries the names.

advanced.description: Keep the default unless a second Home Assistant, or the repository's command-line tools, also join this installation: each needs an address of its own.

reconfigure.title: Update the JUNG HOME mesh export
reconfigure.description: Use this after re-provisioning or re-wiring devices in the JUNG HOME app, or after a key refresh: provide a new export of the same network. Devices that disappeared from the export are removed. Home Assistant's own mesh address can be changed at the same time.

gateway_certificate.title: Gateway certificate changed
gateway_certificate.description: The JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} now presents certificate {observed}; the entry recorded {expected}. Continue only if you replaced the gateway or its certificate yourself — otherwise another device on your network is answering as the gateway.

reauth_confirm.title: Grant Home Assistant access to the gateway again
reauth_confirm.description: The JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} no longer accepts the access Home Assistant registered for the mesh {title} (it was probably removed in the JUNG HOME app under Settings → Gateway → Access permissions). The devices keep working over Bluetooth; only handing Home Assistant's changes to the gateway has stopped. Enter the gateway's network-key password (from the JUNG HOME app) for immediate access, or leave it empty and approve the access request in the app after you continue (Settings → Gateway → Access permissions → Open requests, within three minutes; it appears as “{user_name}”). Only the access is renewed: the export is not fetched again.

data_description.gateway_password: Optional. With it the gateway grants access immediately; without it you approve the request in the app. It is not stored.

areas.title: Rooms and areas
areas.description: Choose the Home Assistant area for each room of the JUNG HOME app. A room is prefilled with the area of the same name, or the area that has the room's name as an alias. Leave a room empty to have an area named after the room (created if there is none). Devices without a room of their own get one too: a push-button's keys the room of the load next to them, a wall transmitter's the room its keys switch. From the Reconfigure menu, this moves the devices that are still in the area the previous choice gave them; a device you placed in another area yourself is never moved.

data.assign_areas: Put the JUNG HOME devices in areas

data_description.assign_areas: Off: new devices start without an area, and the rooms below are ignored.

progress.waiting_for_approval: Open the JUNG HOME app and approve the access request “{user_name}” under Settings → Gateway → Access permissions → Open requests. The gateway at {host} waits up to three minutes.

error.cannot_load: The mesh export could not be read. Check that the file is the app's JSON export (and, for a path, that the path is correct).

error.export_keys_stale: Devices of this mesh are visible over Bluetooth, but none advertises the network key in this export: the network's keys were renewed (a key refresh in the JUNG HOME app) after the export was made. Export the network again from the JUNG HOME app, or fetch it from the gateway again, and use that file.
error.network_mismatch: The export belongs to a different mesh network than the one that was discovered.
error.mesh_already_configured: This mesh is already set up as another entry (its network key has probably been refreshed since Home Assistant last saw it). Use that entry's Reconfigure instead of adding a new one.
error.invalid_host: Enter the gateway's IP address or hostname.
error.cannot_connect: The gateway could not be reached at that address.
error.invalid_auth: The gateway rejected the network-key password.
error.token_rejected: The gateway no longer accepts the stored access. Submit again to request access anew.
error.not_approved: The access request was not approved in the app in time. Submit again and approve it under Settings → Gateway → Access permissions → Open requests.
error.no_project: The gateway holds no network export. Open the JUNG HOME app once while it is connected to the gateway (it uploads the project automatically), and make sure the gateway firmware is 2.1 or newer.
error.gateway_error: The gateway answered with an error. Check its status in the JUNG HOME app and try again.
error.gateway_busy: The gateway is busy with another configuration request. Try again in a minute.
error.upload_failed: The uploaded file could not be processed. Try uploading it again.
error.cannot_store: The export could not be written to the Home Assistant configuration directory.
error.invalid_export: The file is not a JUNG HOME mesh export (or it is damaged): it must contain the network with its keys, nodes and one network key at index 0.

abort.not_jung: This Bluetooth Mesh proxy does not advertise JUNG manufacturer data: it is not a JUNG HOME device.
abort.network_mismatch: The export belongs to a different mesh network than this entry.

abort.certificate_vouched_by_mesh: The JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} presents certificate {observed}, but the gateway node vouched for {expected} over the mesh. If you replaced the gateway or its certificate yourself, reconfigure again while Home Assistant is connected to the mesh: the gateway node then reports the new certificate.

abort.not_loaded: The integration is not running: set it up again first.
abort.not_junghome_gateway: This device does not announce itself as a JUNG HOME Gateway (no JUNG manufacturer or no serial number).
abort.not_ipv4_address: The gateway announced no IPv4 address. Add the integration by hand and enter the gateway's address.

data_description.click_delay: A `click` event is held back for half a second and dropped when a second click follows, so a double press fires only `double_click`. Off: every press fires `click` at once and the second press of a double press fires `double_click` as well. This applies to every key; to wait on some keys only, leave it off and pick them in the list below.
data_description.double_click_keys: Only these keys hold their `click` back for half a second and drop it when a second click follows, so a double press fires only `double_click`; every other key fires `click` at once. Pick the keys that have a double-click automation. Only keys that can click are listed. Unverified on air.
data_description.heartbeats: Every mains-powered device is asked to send a heartbeat to Home Assistant every 64 seconds (a standard Bluetooth Mesh setting the JUNG app leaves off). A device that sends nothing for about three and a half minutes has its entities marked unavailable until it is heard again. Switching this off tells the devices to stop (again on the next connection if they could not all be told at once); switch it off before removing the integration, which cannot tell them afterwards.
data_description.allow_provisioning: Lets the `junghome_ble.add_device` action provision a new JUNG device and configure it as the app would, after a device of the same product already in the network, and `junghome_ble.remove_device` reset a device and take it out of the network. Not tried on real devices yet: try it with a spare device first. Adding hands the device the network's keys; removing cannot be undone.
data_description.provisioner_identity: Every file Home Assistant writes or hands to the gateway gets a provisioner entry for Home Assistant, with address ranges of its own clear of the app's and Home Assistant's address inside them, and the devices Home Assistant added and the app's file lacks are put back. Rooms, scenes and devices Home Assistant creates then take their addresses from its own ranges. No JUNG app has imported such a file yet: try it on a spare app install (import the file from `junghome_ble.export_network`) before your own app or gateway sees it. Off: the files are written exactly as without it.
data_description.follow_app: When the phone running the JUNG HOME app is heard on the mesh, an entry set up from the gateway fetches the gateway's export a few minutes after the phone went quiet (at most every 15 minutes) and takes it over when it changed: devices, rooms, scenes and key connections changed in the app reach Home Assistant without Reconfigure. An entry set up from a file shows a repair notice instead, once the app was seen changing a device's configuration. Nothing is sent on the mesh for it. Unverified on air.
data_description.gateway_check: An entry set up from the gateway asks the gateway for its export every six hours and takes it over when it changed, which catches what the app changed while Home Assistant did not hear the phone. One request to the gateway; nothing is sent on the mesh. No effect on an entry set up from a file.
data_description.sync_areas: When a device changes room in the app (once Home Assistant follows the new export) or through a room action, it moves to the new room's area too — unless you placed it in an area yourself. Off: a device stays in the area it started in. Unverified on air.

service_export_load_failed.message: The mesh export {path} could not be read: {error}

led_colour_unknown.message: The LED colours of {entity} are not known yet; the device did not answer the read.

service_unknown_scene.message: No scene "{scene}" exists in the mesh export; give the scene's name as the JUNG HOME app shows it, or its number.

service_scene_range_full.message: No free scene number is left in the app's range; delete an unused scene first.

service_room_range_crowded.message: Home Assistant gives new rooms the highest free group addresses of the app's range, so that the app's own next rooms do not get the same ones; only {free} free addresses are left below the next one, and the app would soon reach it. service_scene_range_crowded.message: Home Assistant gives new scenes the highest free scene numbers of the app's range, so that the app's own next scenes do not get the same ones; only {free} free numbers are left below the next one, and the app would soon reach it. Delete unused scenes, or turn on the provisioner identity option, which gives Home Assistant a range of its own.

add_device_groups_crowded.message: The new device's element groups would take the highest free group addresses of the app's range, but only {free} free addresses are left below them, and the app's own next rooms would soon reach them. Delete unused rooms, or turn on the provisioner identity option, which gives Home Assistant a range of its own.

service_not_a_scene_element.message: Element {address} cannot store scenes (it has no Scene Setup Server).

service_scene_no_capacity.message: Device {address} has no room for scene {scene}: it already holds {capacity} scenes, timer scenes included. Remove it from another scene first. {applied}

service_scene_not_deleted.message: Device {address} still holds scene {scene} after the delete ({status}). {applied}

service_gateway_export_unavailable.message: The JUNG HOME Gateway did not hand out its export, and this action needs it: the copy Home Assistant keeps may lack what the JUNG HOME app changed since. Try again when the gateway answers (the log says why it did not).

service_unused_scenes_stale_export.message: This network was set up from a file, which may lack scenes made in the JUNG HOME app since it was exported; deleting the scene numbers the file does not know would delete those scenes from every device. Run a dry run first and check the numbers it lists against the app, then delete with "The mesh export is current" on, or name the numbers to delete.

service_unused_scenes_known.message: Scene numbers {numbers} are scenes of the mesh export; delete those with Delete scene.

service_scene_action_not_applied.message: Device {address} stored scene {scene} but did not take the scene description (Scene Action Setup). {applied}

service_scene_state_unknown.message: The state of {address} is not known, so scene {scene} would be stored without its scene description, and taking another channel of the device out of the scene would then drop this one too. service_no_gateway.message: This network was not set up from a JUNG HOME Gateway (no gateway address and token in the entry); reconfigure the entry from the gateway to sync it.

service_gateway_sync_failed.message: The gateway at {host} did not take the export: {error}.

service_send_failed.message: The connection to the JUNG mesh was lost while {message} was being sent to node {node}. {applied}

service_export_unknown_node.message: Node {node} is in the mesh export {path} but not in the network Home Assistant loaded from it earlier; reload the integration (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reload) so it follows the export, then retry. {applied}

service_gateway_export_newer.message: The JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} holds a newer export ({gateway}) than the file Home Assistant would upload ({file}); uploading it would erase what the JUNG HOME app changed since. The next change made in Home Assistant takes the gateway's export over and carries Home Assistant's own changes onto it. service_gateway_export_incomplete.message: The JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} answered with the bare device database only (no device names or room links); adopting it would erase them from the file Home Assistant keeps. Try again once the gateway is no longer busy, or fetch the app's export again.

confirm.title: Skip ahead past the numbers the devices know
confirm.description: Home Assistant hears the JUNG HOME mesh {title} through its proxy node, but not one device answered its state requests. The nodes are discarding Home Assistant's messages as replays. Two causes are likely: the sequence-number store of this integration (`.storage/junghome_ble.*`) was lost or restored from an older backup, so Home Assistant now sends sequence numbers the nodes have already seen; or another mesh client (for example the `mesh_poc.py` tool) transmits with the same unicast address {unicast}. Either give Home Assistant a fresh, unused address (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure → Advanced → Our unicast address, and make sure no other client uses it) or, if the store was lost or restored (and no other client uses the address), confirm to let Home Assistant jump its sequence numbers 1 048 576 ahead and reconnect. Do not restore the sequence-number store from a backup to fix this: an older copy only repeats numbers the devices have already seen. The issue clears itself as soon as a device answers Home Assistant again.

confirm.title: Skip past the other client's sequence numbers
confirm.description: Home Assistant received a message of the JUNG HOME mesh {title} sent from its own unicast address {unicast} with a sequence number it never used: another mesh client transmits with the same address — a second Home Assistant installation, the `mesh_poc.py` tool configured with this address, or a copy of this installation started elsewhere. Two senders on one address reuse each other's sequence numbers, and the devices discard whatever lies below the other client's, so Home Assistant sends nothing to the mesh until this is repaired (commands fail, states are not refreshed). Stop the other client, or give it or Home Assistant another unused address (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure → Advanced → Our unicast address). Then confirm to let Home Assistant continue its sequence numbers past the ones the other client was seen with and send again. If the other client keeps sending from this address, the issue comes back. Do not restore the sequence-number store from a backup to fix this. Unverified on air: a second client on Home Assistant's address has only been simulated.

confirm.description: Home Assistant skipped past the sequence numbers of another mesh client on its address {unicast} in the JUNG HOME mesh {title}, and the other client has sent from that address again since: it is still running. Skipping ahead does not help while it does. Give Home Assistant a fresh, unused unicast address (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure → Advanced → Our unicast address), or stop the other client or move it to another address. Until then Home Assistant sends nothing to the mesh. Confirm only once the other client no longer uses this address: Home Assistant then continues past its numbers again and resumes sending. Unverified on air: a second client on Home Assistant's address has only been simulated.

bluetooth_unavailable.title: No Bluetooth for the JUNG HOME mesh
bluetooth_unavailable.description: The JUNG HOME mesh {title} is reached over Bluetooth, but Home Assistant has no connectable Bluetooth adapter or proxy left: the adapter is switched off, unplugged or has failed, or every ESPHome Bluetooth proxy with active connections is offline. All devices of the mesh are unavailable until one is back. Check Settings → Devices & services → Bluetooth. The issue clears as soon as a Bluetooth adapter or proxy is available again.

duplicate_mesh.title: Two entries cover the same JUNG HOME mesh
duplicate_mesh.description: {title} and {others} are both set up for the same JUNG HOME mesh. They share its sequence-number counters (`.storage/junghome_ble.seq.*`), so only one of them can run: {others} is running and {title} was not started. Remove one of these entries (Settings → Devices & services); if you remove {others}, reload {title} afterwards.

gateway_import.title: Take over the JUNG HOME Gateway integration's entities
gateway_import.description: The JUNG HOME Gateway integration is set up next to the Bluetooth Mesh integration {title}, so every light, socket, key and scene exists twice. Move the gateway entities here — they keep their entity IDs, names, areas and history — under Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME Bluetooth Mesh → Reconfigure → Import the entities of the JUNG HOME Gateway integration, then delete the gateway entry. Ignore this issue if you want to keep both.

export_stale.title: JUNG HOME mesh keys have changed

gateway_refetch.title: Fetch the export from the gateway again
gateway_refetch.description: Home Assistant is connected to a node of the JUNG HOME mesh {title}, but nothing it hears can be decrypted with the keys from the export: every network message and the node's beacon fail authentication. The mesh completed a key refresh (a "key renewal" in the JUNG HOME app) after that export was made, so the file is stale. Confirm to fetch the current export from the JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} with the access Home Assistant already holds, check it and set the integration up again from it, as Reconfigure → Fetch it again from the gateway does; the export it replaces is kept as a copy (`.pre-reconfigure`). The issue clears as soon as a message decrypts again. Unverified on air.

upload.title: Load a new export
upload.description: Home Assistant is connected to a node of the JUNG HOME mesh {title}, but nothing it hears can be decrypted with the keys from the export: every network message and the node's beacon fail authentication. The mesh completed a key refresh (a "key renewal" in the JUNG HOME app) after that export was made, so the file is stale. Export the network from the JUNG HOME app (Project → Share via file) and upload the file here: Home Assistant checks it, keeps it under `junghome_ble/` in its configuration directory (it holds every mesh key) and sets the integration up again from it; the export it replaces is kept as a copy. An entry that read its export from a path on the host uses the uploaded copy from then on — to keep the path, copy the new file there instead and use Reconfigure. The issue clears as soon as a message decrypts again. Unverified on air.

error.address_in_use: In the new export a node has Home Assistant's address, so the entry cannot use it. Give Home Assistant a free address first (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure → Advanced → Our unicast address), then load the export there.

abort.certificate_changed: The gateway at {host} presents another certificate than the one Home Assistant pinned for it: nothing was sent to it and nothing changed. gateway_certificate_changed.title: JUNG HOME Gateway certificate changed
gateway_certificate_changed.description: The JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} no longer matches the TLS certificate Home Assistant pinned for it: the host presents another certificate, or the gateway node reports another one over the mesh. Home Assistant stopped using the gateway (no access token and no export is sent there); devices keep working over Bluetooth. If you replaced the gateway or its certificate, open Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure and fetch the export from the gateway again; otherwise another device on your network may be answering as the gateway — check your network.

gateway_sync_failed.title: JUNG HOME export not handed to the gateway

confirm.title: Hand the export to the gateway
confirm.description: Home Assistant changed the JUNG HOME installation (a room, key connection or scene) and rewrote its mesh export, but the JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} did not take the new export: {error}. Until it does, the gateway and the app show the old state — and the app's next change would overwrite Home Assistant's. Home Assistant tries again twice, 15 seconds apart, as the app does. Check that the gateway is reachable, then confirm to hand it the export now, as the action Sync gateway (`junghome_ble.sync_gateway`) does: it refuses when the gateway holds changes Home Assistant has not seen, which uploading would erase. The issue clears when an upload succeeds. Unverified on air.

The mesh export and the app keep the device's old name. Enter a name the app accepts: Home Assistant names the device with it and passes it on to the export (and with a gateway, to the app) as every rename. The issue clears when the name is passed on. vault_key_refresh_lagging.title: Devices Home Assistant added missed the new network key
vault_key_refresh_lagging.description: The JUNG HOME app renewed the network key of the mesh {title}, and Home Assistant followed the renewal to its end. The app does not know the devices Home Assistant added, so Home Assistant hands them the new key itself, but the device(s) at {addresses} did not confirm it. Make sure they are powered and in range: Home Assistant tries again with every new Bluetooth connection. A device that never received the new key cannot be reached any more: factory-reset it, then add it again (remove it from Home Assistant first with `junghome_ble.remove_device` or `junghome_ble.reset_pending_device`, with `force`). Not yet tried on a real device. The issue clears when every such device confirmed.

pending_device.title: A device Home Assistant added is not recorded
pending_device.description: Home Assistant provisioned a JUNG device of the mesh {title} with `junghome_ble.add_device`, but its configuration or its recording in the export failed: the device at {addresses} has the network's keys, the JUNG HOME app and the export do not know it, and its addresses and element groups stay reserved so no other device gets them. Reset it with the action `junghome_ble.reset_pending_device` (its unicast address) and add it again; for a device you already reset by hand, or one that is gone, use `force`. Not yet tried on a real device. The issue clears when no such device is left.

vault_unwritable.title: JUNG HOME device keys cannot be saved
vault_unwritable.description: Home Assistant could not write its vault for the mesh {title} ({path}; last error: {error}) while adding the device at {address}. The vault holds the device keys of the devices Home Assistant adds, which nothing else has until the export records them, so the device was not provisioned: it received nothing and is still new. This usually means the disk is full or its filesystem was remounted read-only, often a failing SD card. Free up space or repair the storage (a filesystem remounted read-only usually needs the host restarted), then add the device again; do not edit, delete or replace the vault's files. Not yet tried on a real device. The issue clears itself as soon as a write of the vault lands.

carry_over_conflict.title: The JUNG HOME app overrode a change Home Assistant made on {title}
carry_over_conflict.description: Home Assistant took over the export the JUNG HOME app last handed to the gateway and carried its own changes onto it, but the app had changed the same entries meanwhile. The app's version is kept for: {paths}. The devices may still hold what Home Assistant had written: {held}. Check those rooms, scenes and connections in the app and in Home Assistant, and set them again from one side. The app does not see what Home Assistant adds until it imports a file. The issue clears with the next takeover of the gateway's export that has no such conflict.

scene_held.title: Devices still hold a deleted JUNG HOME scene on {title}
scene_held.description: A scene was deleted with "Even if a device does not answer" while some of its devices could not be reached or refused; they still hold it and recall it with any scene of that number. Scene number: devices — {members}. Home Assistant gives no new scene these numbers. When the devices are reachable again, run the action Delete unused scenes with "Dry run" off: it deletes those numbers from them and the issue clears.

gateway_token_rejected.title: JUNG HOME Gateway no longer accepts Home Assistant
gateway_token_rejected.description: The JUNG HOME Gateway at {host} rejects the access Home Assistant registered for the mesh {title} (it was probably removed in the JUNG HOME app under Settings → Gateway → Access permissions). Home Assistant keeps changing rooms, key connections and scenes in its own export, but no longer hands it to the gateway, so the app does not see those changes; the devices keep working. Home Assistant asks for access again: follow its request to re-authenticate JUNG HOME (Settings → Devices & services; Repairs also lists it as expired authentication) and enter the gateway's network-key password or approve the new access request in the app. The issue clears once the gateway accepts Home Assistant again; the action Sync gateway then hands over the changes made since.

restore_too_old.title: Restored backup too old for the JUNG HOME mesh {title}
restore_too_old.description: Home Assistant was restored from a backup, and at the rate Home Assistant's address {unicast} sends, the sequence numbers it may have used since that backup was taken reach the end of the numbers of the mesh's current IV index. Sending again would reuse numbers the devices already saw: they would ignore Home Assistant, and every reused number weakens the mesh's encryption. So Home Assistant sends nothing to the mesh until one of these is done: an IV Update of the mesh — start one with the action `junghome_ble.start_iv_update` (*Developer tools → Actions*, with `confirm: true`; it cannot be undone; Home Assistant sends again once the mesh is at an IV index it cannot have sent under, which after a restore can take two IV Updates in a row) — or a unicast address Home Assistant has never used, set under *Reconfigure*. Do not restore the sequence-number store from another copy. The notice clears itself once Home Assistant can send again. Unverified on air.

seq_store_lost.title: Sequence numbers of the JUNG HOME mesh {title} lost

confirm.title: Continue past the numbers already sent
confirm.description: The sequence-number store of this integration (`.storage/junghome_ble.seq.*`) holds no usable record for Home Assistant's address {unicast}, although that address has sent before. Starting it at 0 again would reuse sequence numbers the devices already saw: they would ignore Home Assistant, and every reused number weakens the mesh's encryption. Restoring the store from a backup does the same — an older copy repeats every number sent since it was taken — so do not restore `junghome_ble.seq.*` files. Confirm to let Home Assistant continue 1 048 576 numbers past the last value it can still read (4 194 304 past the floor it keeps up with the counter in `junghome_ble.seq.*.floor`, or past 0, when none is left) and set the integration up again.

abort.entry_gone: The JUNG HOME entry this issue belongs to is no longer set up.
abort.floor_not_written: The sequence-number floor (`.storage/junghome_ble.seq.*.floor`) could not be written: nothing was changed and the integration stays stopped. Check the disk Home Assistant's configuration is on, then repair the issue again.

seq_store_unwritable.title: JUNG HOME sequence numbers cannot be saved
seq_store_unwritable.description: Home Assistant has not been able to write the sequence-number store of the mesh {title} for over a minute ({path}; last error: {error}). Every message to the devices carries a new sequence number, and Home Assistant only sends numbers it has saved, so that a restart never repeats one: until a write succeeds it sends nothing to the mesh — commands fail and the state is not refreshed. This usually means the disk is full or its filesystem was remounted read-only, often a failing SD card. Free up space or repair the storage (a filesystem remounted read-only usually needs the host restarted); do not edit, delete or replace the store's files. The issue clears itself as soon as a write lands and sending resumes.

address_in_use.title: Home Assistant's JUNG HOME address is taken

confirm.title: Move Home Assistant to {suggestion}
confirm.description: In the export of the mesh {title}, a node occupies the unicast address {unicast} that Home Assistant sends from. Both would be taken for one sender: the devices drop one of them as a replay, and answers go to the wrong one. Confirm to give Home Assistant the free address {suggestion} and set the integration up again, as Reconfigure → Advanced → Our unicast address does. Make sure no other mesh client (the command-line tools of this integration, another Home Assistant) sends from {suggestion}. Sequence numbers are kept per address: the new one continues its own record, or starts far enough in when Home Assistant has none for it, so no number is sent twice. Unverified on air.

abort.cannot_load: The entry's export could not be read, so no free address can be worked out: nothing changed. Load a new export under Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure.
abort.no_free_address: The export leaves no address free for Home Assistant: nothing changed. Check the export under Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure.
abort.address_taken: {suggestion} is no longer free in the export (it changed meanwhile): nothing changed. Repair the issue again for a new suggestion.

address_reserved.title: Home Assistant's JUNG HOME address may be handed out
address_reserved.description: The unicast address {unicast} that Home Assistant sends from in the mesh {title} lies inside the address range of one of the app's provisioners, or was used by a removed node. It keeps working until the app provisions a node there; move Home Assistant to a free address before that (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure → Advanced → Our unicast address; {suggestion} is free).

sequence_space_low.title: JUNG HOME mesh sequence numbers running low
sequence_space_low.description: In the mesh {title}, {source} has used {percent} % of the sequence numbers of IV index {iv_index}. A sender cannot go past the end of that space until the mesh moves to the next IV index (an IV Update). Bluetooth Mesh expects a device that runs low to start that update itself; whether JUNG HOME devices do is not yet known. Home Assistant follows an IV Update, and an administrator can have it start one with the action `junghome_ble.start_iv_update` (it cannot be undone; unverified on air). Every restart of a device (a power cut, a tripped breaker) skips its sequence numbers far ahead, so a device that often loses power runs low first. The issue clears itself after the update.

iv_update_not_taken.title: JUNG HOME mesh did not take the IV Update
iv_update_not_taken.description: Home Assistant started an IV Update of the mesh {title} to IV index {iv_index} at {started}, and the mesh did not take it within 144 hours: the device Home Assistant is connected through still announces IV index {mesh}. Home Assistant has gone back to IV index {mesh} and normal operation; it sent nothing under the new index, so nothing is lost. A device refuses an IV Update within 96 hours of its own last one, and whether JUNG HOME devices take one from Home Assistant at all is unverified on air. While the repair *JUNG HOME mesh sequence numbers running low* is open, the action `junghome_ble.start_iv_update` can try again later. The issue clears itself with the next IV Update.

iv_index_mismatch.title: JUNG HOME mesh is at another IV index
iv_index_mismatch.description: The mesh {title} is at IV index {mesh}, Home Assistant's sequence-number store at {ours}: too far apart for Home Assistant to follow (it follows the mesh up to 42 ahead, at most once every 192 hours, and never back). The devices ignore Home Assistant meanwhile. This happens when Home Assistant was away through many IV updates, when its store (`.storage/junghome_ble.seq.*`) belongs to another mesh, or when beacons forged with the network key pushed it ahead. Give Home Assistant a new unicast address (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure → Advanced → Our unicast address): it starts from the mesh's IV index there. Do not restore the store from a backup or edit it: an older or edited record repeats sequence numbers the devices already saw, and the next start overwrites a hand edit anyway. The issue clears itself when a beacon within reach arrives.

iv_index_ahead.title: Home Assistant is ahead of the JUNG HOME mesh's IV index

confirm.title: Go back to the mesh's IV index
confirm.description: The mesh {title} is at IV index {mesh}, Home Assistant's sequence-number store at {ours} — ahead of it, which the mesh never is: the devices ignore Home Assistant, and it cannot follow a mesh that is behind it. This happens when its store (`.storage/junghome_ble.seq.*`) belongs to another mesh, or when beacons forged with the network key pushed it ahead. Confirm to take Home Assistant back to the mesh's IV index and set the integration up again: its sequence numbers continue above every number it sent from that index on, so none is used twice. Do not restore the store from a backup or edit it instead: an older or edited record repeats numbers the devices already saw. The other way back is a new unicast address for Home Assistant (Settings → Devices & services → JUNG HOME → Reconfigure). Unverified on air: an IV index ahead of the mesh has not been seen on a real one.

abort.entry_gone: The JUNG HOME entry this issue belongs to is no longer set up.

abort.seq_store_not_written: The sequence-number floor (`.storage/junghome_ble.seq.*.floor`) could not be written: nothing was changed. Check the disk Home Assistant's configuration is on, then repair the issue again.

time_keeper_missing.title: JUNG HOME pucks have no time keeper
time_keeper_missing.description: The mesh {title} has JUNG actuator pucks of the older kind ({pucks}): they take their time from a time keeper, a mains device that relays the time to them. No device of the mesh is one, so the pucks' timers drift. Turn on the switch *Time keeper* (a configuration entity, disabled by default) of one device that is always powered, such as a socket or a mini actuator; the JUNG HOME app chooses one itself when it configures a puck. Unverified on air. The issue clears once a device is the time keeper.

A device whose configuration fails is reset, as the app does. Its element groups take the highest free group addresses of the app's range (the app does not see the device until it imports a file). The response lists the steps done. Needs the entry's *Allow Home Assistant to add and remove devices* option. Administrators only. The authenticated methods, the configuration rules and the reset are unverified on air.

start_iv_update.name: Start IV Update
start_iv_update.description: Has Home Assistant start an IV Update of the mesh: the mesh moves to the next IV index, which gives every sender a fresh sequence-number space. Bluetooth Mesh expects a device that is running out of sequence numbers to start one itself; use this when the repair *JUNG HOME mesh sequence numbers running low* stays open. It cannot be undone (the IV index only goes up), and the mesh returns to normal operation 96 to 144 hours later. Refused unless a sender has used three quarters of its sequence numbers (or *Even if not needed* is on), without a connection to the mesh, during a renewal of the network key and within 96 hours of the last start or end of an IV Update. Administrators only. Unverified on air.

abort_iv_update.name: Abort IV Update
abort_iv_update.description: Gives up an IV Update that Home Assistant started and the mesh has not taken yet: Home Assistant goes back to the IV index the mesh is at and stops announcing the new one. Nothing was sent under the new index, so nothing is lost; Home Assistant gives such an update up by itself 144 hours after its start. Refused once the mesh has taken the update (it cannot be undone then), without a connection to the mesh, and before Home Assistant has heard the mesh's IV index on that connection. Administrators only. Unverified on air.

The file holds every key of the installation: delete it once it is imported or stored safely. Administrators only. Importing the file into the app is unverified with the app.
